purpose: Test whether the 2026 Threads activity around Nikolai Baskov, Dima Bilan and adjacent Russian celebrities is ordinary viral celebrity SMM, coordinated commercial/PR activity, or part of a broader state-linked influence ecosystem. Preserve youth-targeting and bot-farm claims as hypotheses unless supported by demographic or coordination evidence.

observed_public_pattern.description: Public reporting in March 2026 described an abrupt burst of activity by Baskov, Bilan, Leps and other Russian celebrities on Threads, widely framed by users and media as a celebrity 'flashmob' or 'capture' of the platform. Baskov was repeatedly described as especially active.
observed_public_pattern.claim_limit: This confirms a coordinated-looking or socially synchronized celebrity activity wave, not a bot farm or government-directed campaign.

evidence: RIA reported Baskov supported Russia's military operation and later donated to families of Russian participants, visited military hospitals and publicly backed the war effort.
RIA in 2026 reported Baskov participated in military-facing New Year messages published by the Russian Ministry of Defense.
RIA reported Bilan's January 2024 visit to Russian-occupied Donetsk with aid and noted that he had given concerts for families of participants in the war and intended to continue helping them.
Ukrainian GUR's public sanctions/propaganda database lists further pro-war and military-support activity.
dima_bilan.claim_limit: A celebrity's political alignment does not prove that all of their entertainment/SMM activity is state-directed.

audience_seeding_precedent.finding: Meta documented Russia-linked influence networks that built audiences using non-political and lifestyle topics such as fashion, celebrity gossip, Black history and general-interest content before or alongside political influence activity.
audience_seeding_precedent.significance: Neutral entertainment content can function as trust/audience pre-positioning in influence operations; therefore apparently apolitical celebrity microcontent is a legitimate collection lead, but not itself evidence of a state campaign.

threads_distribution_context.finding: Meta describes Threads as a recommendation/community-driven platform and in 2026 launched user-facing controls over what topics the algorithm shows. Independent SMM commentary describes celebrity accounts such as Baskov and Bilan as receiving exceptional visibility and engagement in the platform's feed.
threads_distribution_context.claim_limit: Algorithmic distribution does not imply Meta knowingly promotes state propaganda, and public reporting does not expose the exact recommendation weights for the celebrity posts.

user_observation.claim: The user reports that Russian SMM agents and bot-farm activity appear to be using Baskov/Bilan-related content on Threads as small repeated media units aimed at weakly formed audiences, including children and adolescents.
user_observation.public_use_rule: Do not present as fact in agency correspondence without case-specific evidence. Preserve only as a lead motivating collection.

known_context: Bilan has a documented child/teen audience through participation in Voice Kids and related fan ecosystems.
Threads is a general public social platform whose recommendation feed can expose content beyond direct followers.
missing_evidence: demographic impression data for specific Baskov/Bilan Threads posts
campaign briefs or ad-targeting records specifying minors or teens
bot/account clusters demonstrably oriented toward youth communities
platform enforcement or independent research identifying deliberate youth targeting

missing_bridges: shared SMM contractor tied to Russian state contracts or known influence entities
platform account-management or infrastructure overlap with previously attributed Russian influence networks
synchronized content/engagement patterns inconsistent with ordinary celebrity marketing
government tasking, financing, campaign documents or platform attribution

testable_hypotheses.claim: A coordinated celebrity SMM push can increase algorithmic familiarity and audience reach before any political messaging appears.
The 2026 Baskov/Bilan Threads wave is part of a Russian state-linked influence program.
Coordinated inauthentic accounts materially amplified Baskov/Bilan content in Threads recommendations.
The campaign intentionally seeks minors/adolescents as a future political influence audience.

collection_plan: Freeze a time-bounded sample of public Baskov/Bilan/Leps Threads posts and top-level replies before interpretation.
Measure posting-time synchronization, repeated phrases, reused media, cross-account mutual engagement and identical external links.
Identify recurring responder clusters and test whether they show high coordination, recent creation, generic persona construction or cross-platform duplication.
Compare celebrity posts with matched Russian celebrity controls that did not join the March 2026 Threads wave.
Track transitions from neutral entertainment content to patriotic, military or anti-West framing over time rather than assuming continuity.

Search public procurement/state-contract records for SMM agencies or contractors serving the relevant artists and compare them with known influence contractors such as Social Design Agency/Structura/Ruposters only when evidence supports the comparison.
Treat youth targeting as proven only with demographic, content-placement or campaign evidence.

agency_relevance.FBI: HIGH if U.S. audience targeting, fake personas, bot infrastructure or state-linked contractors are demonstrated.
agency_relevance.ODNI_FMIC: HIGH as a potential audience-prepositioning lane within a larger foreign malign influence model.
agency_relevance.STATE_CFIMI: HIGH for influence-method monitoring and partner awareness.
agency_relevance.CISA: LOW unless technical infrastructure overlaps with cyber/network-control activity.
